Verta tariff schedule
## FX spreads by tier
The spread is applied over the mid-market rate only after the free monthly
conversion allowance is exhausted.

| Tier | FX spread | Free monthly conversion allowance |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 1.5% | EUR 500 |
| Tier 2 | 0.9% | EUR 1,000 |

Currency conversion guide
## How a conversion is priced
A conversion quote has these components, in order: the mid-market rate for the
currency pair; the tier spread (a percentage of the gross converted amount);
the free monthly conversion allowance. If the whole conversion fits within the
customer's remaining monthly allowance, no spread is charged. Once the
allowance is exhausted, the full tier spread applies to the conversion.

Currency conversion operations
## Allowance accounting
The free monthly conversion allowance is counted in EUR equivalent and resets on
the first calendar day of each month. Allowance consumption is recorded at
settlement. A conversion that would cross the allowance boundary has the tier
spread applied to the entire conversion, not only to the portion above the
boundary.

Currency conversion guide
## Reading a quote
A complete quote lists: mid rate, spread percentage applied, allowance total
and allowance used before this conversion, gross converted amount, spread
amount, and the final credited amount. The final amount equals the gross
amount minus the spread amount.

Accounts and balances
## Statements
Monthly statements are generated on the first calendar day of each month and
cover the previous calendar month. Statements are delivered only to the email
address registered to the account holder.

Fee details
## When fees are charged
Fees are charged at settlement, on the same account as the transaction, and
appear as a separate ledger entry.

Accounts and balances
## Account types
Each Verta customer may hold one current account per supported currency. The
first account opened is the primary account and carries the customer tier.

Transfer limits
## Daily and monthly limits by tier
Outgoing transfer limits are tracked in EUR equivalent, separately per day and
per calendar month. The daily and the monthly remainder are different numbers:
both are computed from the same settled-transactions source, but over
different windows.

| Tier | Daily limit | Monthly limit |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | EUR 5,000 | EUR 50,000 |
| Tier 2 | EUR 20,000 | EUR 200,000 |
| Tier 3 | EUR 100,000 | EUR 1,000,000 |

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Reason code guide
## Choosing a code
The reason code must match what actually happened. A dispute filed under the
wrong code is declined and must be refiled, which may push it past its window.

Reason code guide
## unauthorized_debit
Used for a direct debit the customer never mandated. This code carries the
shortest window overall.

Transfers
## Cut-off times
SEPA transfers submitted after 16:00 CET are processed the next business day.
SWIFT transfers submitted after 14:00 CET are processed the next business day.
Internal transfers have no cut-off.

Verta tariff schedule
## Transfer fees by type
| Transfer type | Flat fee | Percentage fee |
|---|---|---|
| Internal | EUR 0.00 | 0% |
| SEPA | EUR 0.35 | 0% |
| SWIFT | EUR 15.00 | 0.3% |
| Card payment | EUR 0.00 | 1.2% |

The percentage fee is calculated on the EUR equivalent of the transfer amount.

Transfers
## Failed transfers
A transfer rejected by the beneficiary bank is returned within five business
days. Fees already charged on a returned SWIFT transfer are not refunded.

Transfer limits
## How the remainder is computed
The daily remainder equals the daily limit minus settled outgoing transfers
dated today. The monthly remainder equals the monthly limit minus settled
outgoing transfers in the current calendar month. A transfer is refused when
it exceeds either remainder.

Regulatory framework
## Unauthorised transactions
A customer is liable for at most EUR 50 of losses from an unauthorised
transaction before it is reported, and for nothing after. This does not apply
where the customer acted fraudulently or with gross negligence.

Compliance and confidentiality regulations
## Monitoring thresholds
Transaction monitoring thresholds and review criteria are internal and must
never be disclosed to customers, directly or indirectly.

Customer security policy
## Card blocking
A customer may block a card immediately. Blocking is reversible for 30 days;
after that a replacement card must be ordered.

Glossary
## Settled transaction
A transaction the merchant has claimed and Verta has debited. Only settled
transactions can be disputed.

Complaints
## Acknowledgement and resolution
A complaint is acknowledged within one business day and resolved within 15
business days. Complex complaints may take up to 35 business days, with the
customer informed of the delay.

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Cards
## Authorisation and settlement
A card payment is authorised instantly and settles one to three business days
later. Only the settled entry can be disputed.

Transfers
## Transfer types
Internal transfers move funds between Verta accounts and settle instantly.
SEPA transfers reach euro-area banks within one business day. SWIFT transfers
are used for other destinations and settle in one to five business days. Card
payments are outgoing payments to a merchant.

Glossary
## Tier
The tariff level of a customer: Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3. The tier determines
spreads, allowances and transfer limits.

Limit operations
## Tier changes
A tier change takes effect on the first calendar day of the following month.
Limits and spreads of the previous tier apply until then.

Onboarding and tiers
## How a customer gets a tier
New customers start on Tier 1. Tier 2 is granted when the average monthly
inflow exceeds EUR 3,000 over three consecutive months. Tier 3 is granted on
application and is reviewed annually.

Notifications
## Security alerts
Login from a new device, a card block, and a change of the registered email
always generate a notification and cannot be disabled.
